## [0.8.0] — 2026-11-04

The loop becomes something you can leave running. `run` now fixes a failed
verify or review instead of stopping at the first one, `work` is the one
command that plans, builds, verifies, reviews and finishes, and the run
records enough for a script - or the person after you - to see what happened.

The loop is now observable and resumable rather than only restartable: a run
leaves evidence, an event log and a record a script can read; a worktree run
can be found after the terminal closes; and a route that died is not retried
blind.

### Added

- **`oc-harness work "<request>"`.** Plan when there is no executable plan,
  then build, verify, review, final verify, final review and summary. Flags:
  `--plan-only`, `--dry-run`, `--branch`, `--commit`, `--worktree`,
  `--allow-dirty`, `--max-tokens`, `--max-task-minutes`, `--final-verify`,
  `--final-review`. It never pushes, opens a pull request or publishes.
- **`oc-harness plan "<request>"`.** The planner's answer is validated before
  it is written: every task needs `files:`, `change:` and a `verify:` that can
  fail. A rejected plan never replaces an existing one. `--print` shows it
  without writing; `--force` replaces an existing plan.
- **`oc-harness status [--json]`.** The last run from `.space/run.json`:
  status, reason, per-task attempts, review rounds and checkpoint commits.
- **Plan preflight.** `run` checks the whole plan before the first agent is
  called: no tasks, a missing verify, a verify that cannot fail, or two tasks
  the parser cannot tell apart all stop the run at exit 2.
- **Fix rounds.** A failed verify is handed back to the build agent with its
  real output; a failed review is handed back with its blockers. Default 2
  rounds each (`--max-fix-rounds`, `--review-fix-rounds`).
- **Final checks.** `--final-verify` runs one command after the last task;
  `--final-review` reviews the whole diff from the run's base commit.
  `.space/summary.md` is written only when both pass.
- **Checkpoints.** `--branch` and `--commit` commit each finished task and
  only the paths it touched. `--worktree` runs in `.space/worktrees/<id>` so
  the project itself is untouched while the run happens.
- **Route failover inside a run.** A spent or unreachable route no longer
  marks the task blocked; `work` retries once per other route in the lane
  chain using `OC_HARNESS_MODEL`, and never on the route that failed.
- **`oc-harness lanes --suggest`.** Names lanes the telemetry says are not
  earning a slot. It reads; it never edits `lanes.json` or a profile.
- **A local profile, `ollama-qwen3-coder`.** Qwen3 Coder 30B served by Ollama
  on localhost: zero egress, zero-retention by construction, no per-token
  cost. Pull it with `ollama pull qwen3-coder:30b`.
- **`npm run test:loop`**, and a named CI step for it: end-to-end scenarios
  through the real CLI with a stand-in `opencode`, covering a fix round, a
  review fix, an out-of-scope edit, a vacuous verify, a token budget and a
  failed final verify.

- **`oc-harness autopilot`**: from an empty directory, initialise a blank
  track, tick the charter, run research/design/decompose, then call
  `work --project`. It refuses an existing `.space` without a `track.json`
  instead of overwriting a hand-written track. `--json` keeps stdout to one
  object; `--dry-run` still runs the model-backed spec steps and only makes the
  final work step a preflight.
- **Milestone gates in the built-in templates.** `blank`, `inventory`,
  `billing` and `existing` now put `- gate: {{test_command}}` on M1 and M2, so
  `spec decompose --milestone M1` works on a freshly initialised project. The
  last milestone may omit its gate because there is no next milestone to gate.
- **`oc-harness finish` runs the real completion gate.** It refuses missing or
  empty plans and unfinished tasks with exit 2, runs the track's acceptance
  command (exit 4 on failure), then the install check (exit 1 on drift), and
  reports the dirty/publish bo

## [0.7.3] — 2026-10-26

Documentation only. No code, config or behaviour changed.

The `0.7.2` tarball was built from `8bf0283`, before the README sentence that
describes `npm run selfcheck` was corrected on `main`. It said the release
check ran last; it runs right after the build, against the tarball that build
produced. `0.7.2` users have the old sentence in `node_modules`; this release
republishes the corrected README.

## [0.7.2] — 2026-10-26

A patch about the release process itself: the checks that decide whether a
release is coherent now live in one command and run in CI.

### Added

- **`npm run release:check`.** It compares `package.json` with both versions
  in `package-lock.json`, the first release heading in this file, an optional
  tag, and the files `npm pack --dry-run` would publish. `--release` requires
  the CHANGELOG heading; `--tag v<version>` requires the tag. It is part of
  `npm run selfcheck`, runs in the test job without `--release`, and runs in
  the publish job with the pushed tag.

### Fixed

- **`CONTRIBUTING.md` asked for two commits and two tags.** `npm version`
  already makes both by default, and the steps after it made a second one. The
  release steps now use `npm version --no-git-tag-version`, verify the tree
  before committing, and tag once.
- **`models.yml` claimed a check it did not run.** The scheduled job reads
  catalogue lifecycle; it cannot see a route that answers 200 with no text.
  The comment now says so and names `eval/models.mjs --free --check`.
- **README named `doctor` as the pre-release check.** It is the online check.
  `npm run selfcheck` is the release gate, and the README now says which is
  which.

### Documentation

- **`MIGRATION.md` covers 0.4.x → 0.7.x.** The config file format survives, but
  the compiler now owns more keys: `run` is build + verify, `--review` exits 5
  on a rejected review, the `build` cap is 120, `doc` and `verify` no longer
  open bash with `"*": "allow"`, denied tool calls are not retried, the
  reviewer moved off the retired `nemotron-3-ultra-free`, and `doctor
  --check-models` checks lifecycle rather than presence.

## [0.7.1] — 2026-10-26

A release about checks that were green while the thing they check was not:
a withdrawn model reported healthy, a lane on a model that cannot do the
lane's job, a config from the previous kit reported as matching the current
profile, and a free route that answered nothing still recommended as a
candidate.

### Fixed

- **`doctor --check-models` read presence, not lifecycle.** models.dev keeps
  a withdrawn model and marks it `deprecated`; the check only asked whether a
  record existed, so a pulled base or fallback rung was reported healthy.
  It now asks `isWithdrawn`, and the message says withdrawn-or-removed.
- **A lane's route was never checked for the job it does.** A live model that
  cannot call tools, a `vision` lane on a text-only model, a missing context
  or output ceiling, and an effort level the model cannot express all passed
  `doctor`. Each is now reported by lane, against the first live rung of the
  chain `install` would use. A level that snaps down is still allowed, because
  that is the documented behaviour; a level that resolves to `null` is not.
- **`verify` compared a hand-written key list.** `harness.kit` had been added
  to the compiler and not to the list, so the live install - compiled by
  0.6.4, still carrying 25 ECC subagents - passed as matching the profile.
  The check now recompiles the profile over the installed file and compares
  every key the compiler owns. A config from an older kit is a note;
  `verify --strict` makes it a failure.
- **The probe could not tell an answer from a spent route.** `eval/models.mjs`
  now classifies `ok`, `empty`, `timeout` and `error`, treats a finished step
  with no text as `empty`, and exits non-zero under `--check`.
- **A free route that answered nothing was still recommended.** Two live
  probes of `nemotron-3-ultra-free` produced no step and no text. The route
  is recorded in `eval/unusable-models.json`; `--free` and `research` skip it
  until it is re-probed, and the standalone profile and its reviewer rung are
  retired. The reviewer lane now runs on GLM 5.3 Flash.

### Added

- `eval/models.mjs --free --list` selects live free routes without spending a
  request and names the ones a probe rejected.
- `eval/graph.mjs` checks the import graph and prints the routing graph:
  `--check` fails on an unresolved import, a module cycle, or a source file no
  entry or test reaches; `--routing` prints profile -> lane -> model with the
  catalogue's verdict on each rung. `--json` and `--dot` are for a machine.
- `npm run graph`, `npm run test:coverage` (85% lines, 70% branches, 80%
  functions), and `npm run selfcheck`, which runs build, typecheck, the suite,
  the graph, `premises`, and a fresh install in a temporary config directory
  ending in `verify --strict`.
- `test/effort.test.js` covers the config mutation directly: the router's
  session model, a lane's preserved model and prompt, a `null` variant
  deleting a stale one, `harness` keys surviving, and health entries keyed by
  provider. `test/trust.test.js` covers a replacement that fails after the
  revoke and has to say the package now has no publisher.
- CI runs `graph`, `test:coverage` and `premises` beside the suite, and the
  install smoke test uses `verify --strict`. A daily `models.yml` job asks the
  live catalogue whether every shipped model is still live.

### Changed

- `fleet-safe` and `fleet-all` are refreshed against the live catalogue:
  `fleet-safe` publishes three effort levels (`low`, `high`, `max`) and
  `fleet-all` no longer claims image attachments on a model that does not
  read them.
- README and `docs/ROUTING.md` quote the current fleet: reviewer on GLM 5.3
  Flash, build and longform on Flint, and the seven lanes that move under the
  zero-retention ceiling.

## [0.7.0] — 2026-10-25

`oc-harness run` now stops for the reasons it already claimed to stop for,
the read-only lanes no longer have a write-capable shell, and the token budget
counts the context a request reads instead of only its uncached part.

### Fixed

- **A denied tool call was fed back as another turn, and the retry spent the
  window.** `experimental.continue_loop_on_deny` was `true`, so opencode
  handed the guard's refusal back to the model and continued the loop. The
  measured session made 138 requests and 7,559,016 context tokens in 29
  minutes on six `shared token window` denials, each retry re-sending the
  whole prompt. The generated config now sets it to `false`, and the guard
  blocks a single request that re-sends more than `OC_HARNESS_TURN_STOP`
  (default 300k) with "do not retry".
- **The in-event shared-window stop did not refuse anything.** When the
  `step-finish` sum crossed `OC_HARNESS_BUDGET_WINDOW_STOP`, the guard set
  `windowSpent` but never set `windowWhy`, so `sharedWindowSpent()` returned
  an empty reason and every tool call was allowed. The reason is set where
  the sum crosses, and the stop is written to the ledger with
  `recordStop()` so a new session cannot outlive the provider's window.
- **A corrupt ledger locked the machine for six hours, or vanished.** It is
  now moved to `budget.json.corrupt` and the window starts empty; the broken
  bytes are kept as evidence. `recordSpend()` and `recordStop()` repair
  before writing instead of reading the corruption as an empty window.
- **The bundled ECC subagents were loaded on every request.** Their
  descriptions came from `prompts/agents/*.txt`, were not lanes, and so were
  not covered by the stale-lane rule. They are removed from the generated
  agent map when that is the prompt, and named in the config header; a
  hand-written agent that reuses that prompt path is removed like the
  bundle's own, while any other prompt is left alone.
- **The token budget undercounted a cached session five to forty times, so it
  never fired.** A `step-finish` part reports `input`, `cache.read`,
  `cache.write`, `output` and `reasoning`. The guard summed `input` alone -
  the part of the prompt that was not cached - while the cached prefix, which
  is what a long conversation actually re-reads, was ignored. One measured
  stream reported 844 uncached tokens against 36,480 cached ones on the same
  step, then 391 against 9,088. The 2M warn and 5M stop were therefore five
  to forty times the real spend, and the provider's window ran out before
  either fired. `requestTokens()` in `src/budget.js` now counts `input + cache.read +
  cache.write` for both the session total and the shared-window ledger; the
  toasts and refusals say "context tokens" because that is what they count.
- **The A/B's `--budget` had the same undercount.** The suite cap summed
  `inputTokens`, so 120 runs reported about 1.3M of spend while their streams
  carried 7.1M. `parseStream` now also returns `contextTokens`, the cap and the
  report use it, and `--rescore` re-reads the old streams to put the corrected
  number on them. `inputTokens` is still recorded so a table can be compared
  with the ones written before this.
- **The test suite wrote to the real window ledger.** `guard-hook.test.js`
  exercised the guard with the default `OC_HARNESS_BUDGET_FILE`, so every test
  run added its 1,500 and 600 tokens to
  `~/.local/state/opencode-harness-kit/budget.json` - the live ledger showed
  twelve test entries and nothing else. The tests now point the ledger at
  their own temporary directory.
- **`--rescore` graded a timeout as a wrong answer.** A run that hit the
  ceiling has a stream that stops mid-sentence, which reads exactly like an
  answer that cited nothing; only the sidecar knows which it was. Four runs
  that timed out at 12 steps were re-scored as four wrong answers, and the
  table then showed 18/23 where the honest count is 18/19.
